build.system: pip/setuptools (setup.py compiles 2 Cython extensions: synapses/cythonspikequeue.pyx, memory/cythondynamicarray.pyx)
commands: # host: ubuntu@EC2 (8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM, Ubuntu 26.04, gcc 15.2.0, python 3.14.4)
cp -r brian2-2.10.1 brian2-build  # scratch copy, pristine checkout untouched
pip install cython pytest pytest-timeout matplotlib scipy
pip install -e brian2-build  # 26 s wall; resolves numpy 2.5.3, cython 3.1.3 (pin is <3.1.4), sympy 1.14.0, jinja2, pyparsing
pitfalls: pyproject pins cython>=0.29.21,<3.1.4; pip resolved 3.1.3, fine today, but a future cython release cannot be picked up

the cython runtime codegen target compiles every generated code object into ~/.cython/brian_extensions on first use: first simulation of a new model pays tens of seconds of gcc time; the cache dir must exist and be writable

landscape.how_to_run: python -m pytest brian2/tests/<file> (config brian2/tests/pytest.ini); official driver brian2.test() repeats the suite per codegen target and phases standalone via markers (codegen_independent, standalone_compatible, standalone_only, multiple_runs, long, openmp, gsl)
landscape.notes: 36 test files, 25189 lines; per-test timeout 3600 s in pytest.ini; reference outputs: none in repo; correctness lives in assertions

landscape.how_to_run: python examples/<name>.py with MPLBACKEND=Agg (all end in matplotlib show())
landscape.notes: 10 top-level classics (CUBA, COBAHH, IF_curve_LIF...), synapses/ 12, compartmental/ 11, advanced/ 9, standalone/ 6, multiprocessing/ 3, frompapers/ 49; reference outputs: none; dev/tools/run_examples.py only smoke-runs them for docs

pitfalls.symptom: 4 schedule-related tests fail and test_magic_network hangs >60 s when the whole file runs in one pytest process (python 3.14.4, numpy 2.5.3); all 5 pass together in isolation in 21 s
pitfalls.workaround: run tests in per-file or per-test pytest processes; do not chain the whole file in one process in this environment

pitfalls.symptom: AssertionError on warning count in full-file order, passes alone (warning registry leaks across tests)

pitfalls.where: cython runtime target (default when a compiler exists)
pitfalls.symptom: first run of any model pays gcc compilation of generated code objects; silent tens of seconds
pitfalls.workaround: warm the on-disk cache, or set prefs.codegen.target='numpy' for compile-free runs

pitfalls.symptom: same brian2.seed() gives different results on runtime vs cpp_standalone device (different RNG streams)
pitfalls.workaround: grade within one target only, or use conftest fake_randn pattern for cross-target checks

pitfalls.symptom: all end in matplotlib show(); block under a display, silent under Agg
pitfalls.workaround: MPLBACKEND=Agg and grade numeric quantities, not figures

need the GNU Scientific Library headers; excluded by the official driver by default
threading mode off by default; grading will pin single thread for determinism
